_doc: Scenarios (fictional). map = map parameters (missing ones take the defaults; layout = a hand-made map from maps.json, which brings its own size); settings = game settings; goal.metric: bookValue | netWorth | bestYearRevenue | cargoLoads (with cargos) | rank (net-worth rank among all investors, lower is better). tiers = [bronze, silver, gold] thresholds. requires = conditions every medal needs (connect = your own track between two towns, by population rank or by name on hand-made maps). years = time limit from the start year; reaching gold earlier ends the scenario early. See BALANCING.md. difficulty = easy | medium | hard (shown in the list). settings.boardVotes = false: the shareholders never vote you out (easy scenarios).

scenarios.name: Tutorial: First Spike
scenarios.brief: Learn the ropes: connect two towns, run a train and earn your first fortune. Step-by-step help guides you.

scenarios.name: The Iron Horse
scenarios.brief: 1835: the first railways are a curiosity. Build a profitable little line and grow the company's book value before 1845.

scenarios.name: River Towns
scenarios.brief: 1840: the valley towns of Twin Rivers trade by barge and cart. Give them a railway and build up the company's book value by 1850.

scenarios.name: Coal for the Mills
scenarios.brief: 1870: the steel mills are hungry. Haul coal, iron and steel — deliver as many loads as you can by 1880. One friendly rival competes for the towns.

scenarios.name: Over the Pass
scenarios.brief: 1858: Wheatfield's grain rots for want of a way to the coast. Drive a line over the High Pass to Port Ashby and make it pay before 1870. A rival has the same idea.

scenarios.name: Black Gold
scenarios.brief: 1895: oil gushes from the sands of the basin. Haul crude to the coastal refineries and petroleum to the towns — as many loads as you can by 1905.

scenarios.name: Bridge the Divide
scenarios.brief: 1880: the two largest towns lie far apart across rough country. Link them with your own track and make the railroad pay before 1892.

scenarios.name: Lake Shore Line
scenarios.brief: 1872: the towns around the Great Lake still trade by steamer. Link Northshore and Southport by rail, outbuild two rivals and grow your own fortune by 1887.

scenarios.name: Streamliner Age
scenarios.brief: 1936: sleek diesels promise speed. Build a fast passenger network and reach the biggest net worth you can before 1950.

scenarios.name: Commuter Rush
scenarios.brief: 1948: the suburbs of Capitol City boom and everyone needs to get downtown. Carry the most passengers and mail by 1958 — two rivals want the same commuters.

scenarios.name: Robber Barons
scenarios.brief: 1885: three ruthless barons want the country for themselves. Outplay them on the rails and on the stock market: be the richest by 1900.

scenarios.name: Coast to Coast
scenarios.brief: 1866: the great race. Join Bayview on the western ocean to Eastport on the eastern one with your own rails, and end up the richest baron on the continent by 1886.
